reason: Directly clones the 195-kb Xq28 region containing the red and green color pigment genes (OPN1LW and OPN1MW) in tandem array; foundational genomic characterization of the OPN1LW locus.

Studies differential regulation of tandemly-duplicated long wavelength-sensitive (LWS) cone opsin genes by retinoic acid in zebrafish; LWS1/LWS2 are the zebrafish orthologs of OPN1LW. Directly addresses opsin gene regulation in cone photoreceptors.

Review of the Elongator complex in neurological disorders (Huntington's disease, familial dysautonomia). ELP4 encodes Elongator subunit 4 (Elp4); a disease-focused review of ELP4's protein complex is directly relevant to ELP4 biology, even though the eye-disease connection is through chromosomal proximity to PAX6 rather than Elongator neurological function.

Population genetics study of the red pigment gene (OPN1LW) molecular abnormalities across Caucasian, Japanese, and Afro-American populations. Directly characterizes OPN1LW gene structure variants and their phenotypic consequences in color vision deficiency.

Classic description of isolated foveal hypoplasia without albinism or aniridia in nine patients with congenital nystagmus. This is precisely the phenotype caused by SLC38A8 mutations; directly defines the clinical entity.

Reviews primate color vision evolution including LWS (OPN1LW) opsin gene allelic differentiation and gene duplication. Directly discusses OPN1LW/LWS gene biology, adaptive significance, and behavioral consequences of opsin variation; relevant for understanding OPN1LW evolutionary context.

First structural model of the Elongator complex (Elp1-6 hexameric assembly) by single-particle EM and cross-linking mass spectrometry. ELP4 is Elongator subunit 4 (Elp4); structural data on the Elongator complex is foundational to understanding ELP4 function and disease mechanisms.

Creates knock-in mice expressing human L-opsin (OPN1LW) variants to study disease-causing cone opsin alleles (blue cone monochromacy, myopia, cone dystrophy). Directly models OPN1LW variant pathophysiology in vivo.
Maps L:M cone opsin mRNA ratio across human and baboon retinas using RT-PCR, demonstrating a central-to-peripheral gradient. Directly characterizes OPN1LW expression topography in human retina.

Measures unique hue wavelengths and relates them to L/M cone ratio (estimated by genetics and ERG flicker photometry), revealing that unique green depends strongly on cone numerosity. Directly implicates OPN1LW/OPN1MW gene-driven cone ratio variation in individual color experience.

Presents Paraphase, a HiFi long-read method for resolving highly similar paralogous genes including OPN1LW/OPN1MW (which form a high-similarity tandem array). The paper explicitly covers medically relevant genes challenging to genotype; directly applicable to OPN1LW clinical genetic testing.

Quantifies individual differences in L-cone (OPN1LW) and M-cone photopigment spectral sensitivities across 51 observers using LED trichromator and CIEPO06 observer modeling. Directly measures OPN1LW photopigment spectral variation relevant to color vision phenotyping.

Measures L:M cone ratios in 60 heterozygous female New World monkeys using ERG flicker photometry; X-linked opsin alleles in these primates are direct homologs of OPN1LW/OPN1MW. Provides quantitative data on opsin-driven cone mosaic variation directly relevant to OPN1LW cone biology.

Characterizes molecular patterns and sequence polymorphisms of the red (OPN1LW) and green (OPN1MW) pigment genes in Japanese males, including haplotypes and recombination hotspots. Directly about OPN1LW gene molecular genetics across populations.

Develops quantitative foveal structural metrics (IRL, OS, ONL ratios) as predictors of visual acuity in albinism-related foveal hypoplasia. SLC38A8 mutations cause isolated foveal hypoplasia; this paper's quantitative characterization of foveal hypoplasia grades and their visual acuity correlates directly informs the SLC38A8 phenotype workup.

Demonstrates that loss of wobble uridine (U34) tRNA modifications (performed by the Elongator complex, of which ELP4 is subunit 4) causes ribosome stalling at suboptimal codon pairs and triggers cellular quality control. Directly characterizes the functional consequences of Elongator/ELP4 deficiency at the molecular level.

Compares performance of protan and deutan carriers (heterozygous for OPN1LW/OPN1MW gene defects) on seven color vision tests including Ishihara plates. Directly characterizes the phenotypic expression of OPN1LW/OPN1MW carrier status in females.

Compares Ishihara/HRR pseudoisochromatic test results with MassArray genotyping of OPN1LW and OPN1MW genes directly. Explicitly names OPN1LW as the target gene; demonstrates that genetic testing identifies twice as many color-deficient males as phenotypic testing alone.

Molecular characterization of a novel single X-linked visual pigment gene with unique exon 5 arrangement (Y277 from L gene, A285 from M gene) causing an atypical dichromatic color vision defect. Directly about OPN1LW gene structure and intragenic recombination causing color vision deficiency.

Case report of surgical repair of myopic macular hole-related retinal detachment in a child with Knobloch syndrome. Knobloch syndrome is caused by COL18A1 mutations; the paper directly describes the ocular phenotype and surgical management of COL18A1-associated disease.
